source_version.content: The historical relationship is turning out to be almost exactly the useful version of your hypothesis: **Kepler accused Fludd of lacking measured motion; Fludd replied that Kepler had captured only the material/quantifiable half of harmony.** So “Fludd finished Kepler’s math” is too strong historically, but **Kepler supplies the metric that Fludd’s symbolic architecture lacks**—and that may be precisely the missing bridge for our Dee/music model.
